description: The line plot illustrates the performance of three methods—TACRED, TACRED-Revisit, and SemEval—measured by Micro F1 percentage across different numbers of samples generated, specifically at K=8, K=16, and K=32. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Samples Generated," is a categorical scale with three distinct points: K=8, K=16, and K=32. The y-axis, labeled "Micro F1 (%)," is a linear scale ranging from 20 to 50, with major gridlines at intervals of 10. The TACRED method, represented by a blue line with circular markers, shows a steady increase in Micro F1 from approximately 25% at K=8 to about 30% at K=32. The TACRED-Revisit method, shown with an orange line and triangular markers, also increases, starting at around 24% at K=8 and rising to approximately 31% at K=32. The SemEval method, depicted by a red line with square markers, exhibits the highest performance, starting at about 42% at K=8, rising to 45% at K=16, and peaking at 52% at K=32. The green line with diamond markers, which corresponds to the TACRED-Revisit method in the legend, appears to be a mislabeled data series, as its values are significantly higher than the other two methods and do not align with the TACRED-Revisit data. The actual TACRED-Revisit data is represented by the orange line. The SemEval method consistently outperforms the other two methods across all sample sizes.
